terms.meaning: a styling library that provides small ready-made style classes
a named value that style rules can reuse
a smooth blend from one colour to another
a colour theme with a dark background, chosen by the device setting

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Tailwind base styles loaded
sections.what: Loads Tailwind's three standard style groups so its ready-made classes work across the site.
sections.why: Likely reason: the components use Tailwind classes, so these must load first.

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Light mode colour values
sections.what: Stores the default text colour and the two background colours as named values for the light theme.
sections.why: Likely reason: named values let the dark mode rule replace them in one place.

sections.name: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
sections.title: Dark mode colour override
sections.what: When the device prefers dark mode, switches the text to white and the backgrounds to black.
sections.why: Likely reason: the theme follows the device setting automatically, with no switch on the page.
sections.watch_out: Text without its own colour turns white, which can be hard to read on the light cards used elsewhere.

sections.name: body
sections.title: Page text and gradient background
sections.what: Sets the default text colour and draws a gradient background. Also defines a small utility that balances text wrapping.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the whole page a consistent backdrop.
sections.watch_out: The page's own wrapper paints its own gradient over this, so some changes here may not be visible.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar
sections.title: Scrollbar width
sections.what: Makes the scrollbar 8 pixels wide and high in Chrome, Edge and Safari.
sections.why: Likely reason: a thinner, consistent scrollbar matches the page look.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-track
sections.title: Scrollbar track background
sections.what: Gives the scrollbar track a light grey background with rounded ends.
sections.why: Likely reason: part of the same scrollbar look.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb
sections.title: Scrollbar handle colour
sections.what: Colours the draggable part of the scrollbar mid grey, with rounded ends.
sections.why: Likely reason: part of the same scrollbar look.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover
sections.title: Scrollbar handle hover colour
sections.what: Darkens the scrollbar handle when the mouse is over it.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows that the handle is active.

summary: Global styling: Tailwind base styles, a background gradient, text colours that switch for dark mode, and a grey scrollbar look.
purpose: Sets the basic look of every page so the background and colours are consistent across the site.
why: Likely reason: styles that apply to all pages are kept in one place.
how: Loads the three Tailwind style groups. Stores the light colours as named values. Replaces them with dark values when the device prefers dark mode. Sets the default text colour and the gradient background. Adds a small text-balance utility. Finally styles the scrollbar in grey.
inputs: The device's dark or light preference, and the Tailwind setup.
outputs: The page background gradient, default text colour, a text-balance utility, and the scrollbar look.
risks: In dark mode the default text becomes white. Text that has no colour of its own and sits on a white card would be hard to read. Scrollbar styling only applies in Chrome, Edge and Safari.
debug: If text is unreadable in dark mode, check the default text colour and whether the element sets its own colour. If the background looks wrong, check the body rule and the Tailwind lines at the top.
